# Dashboard & Alerts

The Dashboard is the first page you see after signing in. It gives a quick picture of inventory, translations, language coverage, and AI usage.

## What The Dashboard Is For

Use the Dashboard when you want a quick answer to: "Is the system healthy today?"

It is not where most work happens. It is the place to notice changes, costs, and problems that need attention.

## What To Check

The Dashboard gives a quick system overview after sign-in.

![Dashboard overview with inventory, category, language, and translation cards](/help-screenshots/dashboard-overview.png)

- Total Categories: how food is grouped.
- Food Items: how many items are being tracked.
- Languages: how many languages are available.
- Translations: how much translated content FEED has produced.
- Charts: inventory mix, category counts, cost, usage, and translation performance.

## When To Use Alerts

Use the alert bell when FEED needs your attention.

Alerts may appear when translation work fails, gets stuck, or needs review. They help staff find issues before a client-facing document or list is needed.

## How To Review Alerts

1. Select the bell in the top-right area.
2. Read the newest alerts first.
3. Follow the action described in the message.
4. Mark alerts as read when they are no longer useful.

## Why Some Charts Are Empty

Empty charts do not always mean something is broken.

On a new setup, FEED may not have enough activity yet to show usage or cost history. Add inventory, translate documents, and generate shopping lists before expecting every chart to fill in.
